[P2] Approach: satisfy rule 4 for the new blocking branches

The wiring test checks only that the gate is awaited before the query call. Removing this early return—or either equivalent return in the other data tools—does not change that assertion, the isolated gate tests, or the existing integration cases, yet permits queries after consent is declined. The new Glue error-handling branches and settings-warning branches also lack behavioral coverage. This breaks rule 4, “Every branch has a test that fails without it,” despite the description's mutation-check claim. Return to the design phase under rule 8, step 6, and agree on observable acceptance cases across the check, gate, tool, and warning UI before revising the implementation.
